t: Born and raised in Stratford-upon-Avon, Shakespeare was a known figure in the London theatre by 1592 and became an actor, writer and part-owner of the leading playing company, which gave him a large estate.
He wrote comedies and histories in the 1590s, mainly tragedies until 1608 and romances in his last phase, and appears to have retired to Stratford around 1613, three years before his death.
Few records of his private life survive, so his religion, his sexuality and his appearance have been argued over, and his friends Heminges and Condell published his plays in the First Folio of 1623.
dyk: The Globe burned to the ground on 29 June 1613 when a cannon fired during a performance of Henry VIII set fire to the thatch, an event that pinpoints the date of a Shakespeare play with rare precision.
ev: Baptised in Stratford-upon-Avon on 26 April; his birthday is traditionally observed on 23 April
Marries Anne Hathaway, who is 26 to his 18; the licence is issued on 27 November and the banns are read once instead of three times
Attacked in print by Robert Greene as an "upstart Crow", the earliest surviving mention of his work in the theatre
A partnership of the company's members builds the Globe on the south bank of the Thames
The Lord Chamberlain's Men receive a royal patent from James I and become the King's Men
Appears to retire to Stratford; his last plays are collaborations, probably with John Fletcher, and the Globe burns down on 29 June
Dies on 23 April, within a month of signing his will, and is buried in the chancel of Holy Trinity Church
John Heminges and Henry Condell publish the First Folio, which contains 36 plays, 18 of them printed for the first time

f.born: Stratford-upon-Avon, Warwickshire; baptised on 26 April 1564, his date of birth unknown but traditionally observed on 23 April; son of John Shakespeare, an alderman and glover, and Mary Arden
f.died: 23 April 1616, at the age of 52, in Stratford-upon-Avon; no extant contemporary source explains how or why he died; buried in the chancel of Holy Trinity Church two days later
f.role: Playwright, poet and actor; sharer in the Lord Chamberlain's Men (from the 1590s) and the King's Men (from 1603); part-owner of the Globe (1599); his company also took over the Blackfriars theatre in 1608
f.known: some 39 plays, among them Hamlet, Othello, King Lear, Macbeth, Romeo and Juliet and The Tempest; 154 sonnets; the narrative poems Venus and Adonis and The Rape of Lucrece; the Globe; the First Folio of 1623, published after his death
